target_customer: Data science and analytics teams, plus students and teachers using notebooks
problem: Data scientists struggle to collaborate in Jupyter notebooks and to set up infrastructure. Deepnote offers a cloud, Jupyter-compatible notebook with real-time collaboration.
business_model: Freemium SaaS per team seat for a collaborative data workspace
product_category: Data science notebook and collaborative data workspace

founders.name: Jakub Jurovych
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Feb 2020) describes him as a former Mozilla engineer who did data science work and helped companies scale data science teams. Name also spelled Jurových.

technical_complexity.rationale: Hosted Jupyter-compatible runtime with real-time collaboration, scheduling and GPU machines; standard cloud engineering with hard multiplayer and infrastructure parts.

defensibility.rationale: Notebook format is open and Jupyter compatible, so copying and switching are easy; defensibility rests on workflow and team data integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hosted notebooks from large players already existed; Deepnote stayed independent, bought Hyperquery in July 2024 and went open source in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch quoted the CEO saying people have real trouble collaborating on data science work, and the product was already popular with students and teachers by February 2020.

identity.logo: Cube graphic noted on the site
identity.visual_style: Terminal style ASCII banners and a cube graphic
identity.voice_and_tone: Humane and explorer themed; original description speaks of data scientists as explorers

branding.brand_signature: Notebook manifesto and the explorers theme
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches in 2020 and 2021; the site claims 600,000 plus data professionals use it.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognizable among data teams with press and Product Hunt presence, but no source shows merch, mascot or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Deepnote joined YC in Summer 2019, emerged from stealth with a 3.8M seed in February 2020 led by Index and Accel, and raised a 20M Series A in January 2022. It reached general availability in 2022, acquired Hyperquery in 2024 and open sourced its notebook later. It remains active with a modest headcount reported in aggregators and no exit.
